findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

An open package of raw ground beef was observed in a cooler drawer alongside an opened package of Ready-To-Eat (RTE) sliced cheese. Juices were observed throughout the bottom of the drawer. The PIC and cook were shown and the foods in the drawer discarded to correct. Education was conducted. Ensure that raw and RTE foods are stored so that cross contamination does not take place.

findings.title: Gloves used properly.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 (A) Glove Use (A) if used, SINGLE-USE gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discard when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation. 

An employee was observed to handle a bluetooth speaker with their gloved hands and then handle ready for service meals and foods. Education was conducted and the PIC was instructed to educate staff as to when gloves should be changed. Change gloves whenever moving between tasks or whenever they may have become contaminated, and prior to handling foods.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

The hand sink next to the mop sink was blocked with a cart and broom. The PIC was shown and moved the items to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

Two containers of milk in a standing cooler are observed with date marks of 3/17-3/31. This is incorrect. Seven day date marking from 3/17 would indicate that the milks should be used or discarded at the end of 3/23 (yesterday). The PIC was shown and education conducted with them and the employee nearby. The milks were discarded to correct. Ensure that date marking is conducted with correct procedures and followed. Ensure that staff is properly training on date marking to prevent future concerns.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day.

1) Two opened gallons of milk in the standing cooler at the end of the prep line are observed without date marking. Neither the PIC or the worker knew when the containers had been opened. 2) A gallon of milk is partially used and bares a date marking of 8/20. This indicates that it should have been discarded at the end of last night at the latest. All three containers of milk were discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Education should trickle down to the employees working in this area to ensure that this situation does not repeat in the future.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Several flies (at least 8-10) are observed by the mop sink and adjacent tanks. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact their pest control agency (EcoLab) for maintinance. They did mention that EcoLab had already been planning on starting a fly based plan in the facility. This should probably be pushed forward and implemented immediately. The normal follow-up schedule would land on a weekend and will be pushed back to the following Monday.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

A piece of equipment next to the grill is observed with encrusted food residue in the gaps/crack provided by cracked aluminum tape. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and then re-seal the spaces prior to the next routine inspection. The PIC then indicated that this equipment was unused and a leftover from when Wahlburger’s was here. He stated that it would be discarded prior to the next inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The hand sink next to the mop sink is observed pulling away from the wall, which is producing a gap that is not easily cleanable. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all facility equipment is maintained in good repair at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Th hand sink next to the mop sink is without paper towels at the beginning of this inspection. The PIC was notified and the paper towel dispenser refilled during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are supplied with needed supplies at all times.

findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

The soda gun in the bar area is observed stored submerged in the ice in the ice bin. The PIC was shown. This item is not regularly cleaned/sanitized on the outside or on the metal hose leading to it. Due to this this item should be stored outside of the ice (a Ready-to eat (RTE)) food to protect it from possible contamination. The gun was removed from the bin to correct.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. 

An employee drink is observed on the shelf above the prep cooler. The PIC was consulted and the drink discarded during this inspection to correct. Ensure that employee foods/drinks are stored seperately from foods or food contact surfaces to prevent possible contamination moving forward. It is preferred that storage is below and/or away from foods and food preparation areas.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

An egg wash is observed on a shelf over raw cut onions in the prep cooler to the left of the grills. Employees believe this to be from the French toast prep during the mornings. The situation was discussed and the containers moved during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

1) The potato slicer in the kitchen area is observed soiled with food debris. The debris is hard, indicating that it has been left for a prolonged period of time without cleaning. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the item moved to dish for cleaning. 2) The cvap equipment is observed soiled during this inspection with food debris/juices that appear to have been there for a significant amount of time. The employee on duty indicated that they used the equipment 2 days ago and do not know if it had been cleaned since that event. It was stated that equipment should be cleaned after use and not allowed to sit while soiled. The employee was observed cleaning the equipment during the inspection to correct.

findings.comment:

All contaminated single service items were discarded and their containers moved to dish for cleaning.

The hand sink next to the mop sink has obvious food debris caked in its basin. Sink is set up as a hand sink and needs to be maintained as a hand sink only (not a dump sink). Sink to be cleaned and used only for hand washing moving foreword.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling in sushi and Kitchen Creations is incomplete. Facility should be indicating the time food is pulled from heat source/past active cooling process(if noodles and using running water)/placed on counter. Monitor time and temperature to insure time/temperature benchmarks are being met. Discussed with staff during inspection. Will spot check to monitor behavior change. Use signage and cooling logs for best practice. 
 Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12  (Pf) Staff in sushi, Hickory House, and Kitchen Creations does not have available thermometers for monitoring cooling and cooking temperatures. A food thermometer is not available. Food thermometers shall be provided and readily accessible to ensure proper food temperatures. Reference 4-302.12.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Observed sushi prep cooler to have food stored in direct contact with white wiping cloths. Wiping cloths are being used to hold moisture. Cease using cloths. Use a paper towel or parchment paper that may be discarded after use. Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Single-service rack on the side of island counter in sushi is observed holding food splash debris between the counter and the top of the rack. Clean this gap. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed lo mein noodles and chicken in the chinese walk-in cooler to be at temperatures of 93-121F at the 2 and 3 hours of cooling. The process is being improperly monitored. No logs were noted and no labeling on the times the food started cooling. All times were by word of mouth from the chef's. Ensure that the process below is followed. Active cooling process does not start until the product reaches 135F. The product may rest on the counter until it reaches close to 135F, then time it and place it in the cooler or freezer for active cooling. Lo mein was at 3 hours so it was discarded. The chicken was reheated to restart the cooling process. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.comment:

Ensure that the container is cleaned as often as necessary and the regularly checked. The ice scoops were removed and sent through dish, as well as the container that holds them.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
1) Observed fried rice, probed at 51F, sitting in the walk-in cooler near the cook line. The fried rice was made last night prior to staff leaving. Fried rice discarded during the inspection. 2) Observed 4 large containers of lo mein noodles, that were made last night, to be probed between 50-52F. The lo mein was discarded during the inspection. Ensure that cooked, PHFs are properly cooled following the guidelines listed below. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the soda gun at the bar to have an excessive accumulation of soda syrup and debris. Ensure that these food contact surfaces are cleaned regularly. If the soda gun is no longer in use, then it should be thoroughly cleaned prior to discontinuing use. Soda gun was cleaned during the inspection. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
1) Observed a container of salsa con queso, that is prepared at room temperature, to be probed at 49F. After discussing the product with the employee and management, it was determined that the product had started cooling 4.5 hours prior to finding the item. Employee and management were told that PHFs, that are prepared at room temperature, are still required to cool to 41F or below within 4 hours of preparation. After checking the salsa and the cheese, it was determined that the product should be discarded. The can of cheese specifically stated on the side that it should be cooled immediately after opening for safety. The cooler was also found to be in defrost for part of the time that the product was cooling in it. Management should make the defrost times of the coolers common knowledge for employees. This will increase cooling by knowing which coolers to utilize for cooling throughout the day. 2) Observed 5 pans of lo mein noodles, probed between 80-100F, cooling in the walk-in cooler by Asian and in the Asian prep cooler. Employee stated they had been made at 1:00 PM. The product was inspected at 2:55 PM. Management was given the option to reheat the product to 165F, then restart the cooling process or to discard the product. Management opted to reheat the product. Ensure that when products are cooling they are uncovered and in shallow pans. The shallow pans is to increase the surface area of the product exposed to cold air. The facility also has a blast chiller that they could utilize for cooling the noodles. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment:
Observed 2 ice scoops that were being stored in a ice scoop holder that was soiled with syrups and food debris. Ensure that the holders for the ice scoops are maintained in a clean and sanitized condition. This is to prevent cross contamination into the ice. Holder and scoops were sent to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed multi-purpose cleaner being stored in crate with other spices and foods to be used for preparation. Ensure that chemicals are properly separated from food/food contact surfaces. The chemical bottle was moved during the inspection. 
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed sliced turkey in a prep cooler on the cook line that was dated 3/25. This is past the 7 day date marking and should have been discarded. Two pans of prepared, sliced turkey were discarded  by the manager. Ensure that refrigerated, ready to eat, PHFs are not used beyond their 7 day date marking. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
1) Observed eggs in their carton being stored in a prep cooler, at the chef's creation station, above bell peppers. Ensure that eggs, and their cartons, are stored below ready to eat foods to prevent cross contamination. 2) Observed a soiled scoop being stored in the BBQ rub that is used on raw meats. The scoop was saturated like it had become moistened when dealing with the meats. The scoop was sent to dish and the BBQ rub was discarded. Ensure that utensils are not stored in product, regularly changed, and if they become contatminated with raw product are not cross contaminating ready to eat product.  
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed a utensil, used for serving pizza, soild with old food debris. Utensil was taken to dish to be washed. Ensure that the utensils are properly cleaned before being placed into service.  
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.comment:

Tomatoes were disposed of. Ensure that PHFs are kept below 41F, or they are time marked and discarded after 4 hours of being out of temperature.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: 1) Observed rice scoop to be stored in water on the wok line. Utensils should be stored in running dipper wells, clean and dry or put on a time control to change the water and wash, rinse and sanitize the utensils every 4 hours. 2) Observed an employee handle bread with her bare hands. Employee was addressed and educated that gloves, tongs, or some sort of barrier must be used to avoid bare hand contact with ready to eat foods. 3) Observed small cups used as dispensing utensils in a container of sesame seed and a container of cashew nuts.  750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells. 750-280 To avoid unnecessary manual contact with food, suitable dispensing utensils shall be used by employees or provided to consumers who serve themselves..

findings.comment:

750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed a soiled knife stored in a soiled knife holder to the side of the prep cooler in the Chinese area. Store utensils clean and dry.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Provide covered waste cans for customer restrooms.
750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:

750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed a container of raw egg mixture stored on an ice bath to be at 60F probed with a recently calibrated metal stem thermometer. Container of egg mixture was discarded. Ice baths shall be a water and ice mixture and completely encompass the food container to ensure it is being maintained at 41F or below. Ice only at the bottom of the container will not maintain foods are 41F or below.
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed a container of chili, soup, and marinara in the steam well to have an internal temperature of 125-130F. Facility stated the steam well often makes food items boil, therefore the unit was just recently turned down and food temperatures dropped below at 135F. Benefit of doubt was given and facility was allowed to reheat these food items to 165F to be maintained on the steam well at 135F.
Monitor temperatures of hot potentially hazardous foods throughout the day to ensure they are being maintained at 135F or above. 750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation

Lids were provided to correct the violations. 750-130(a) Food shall be stored in clean, covered containers once being removed from the original package. 750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Wash, rinse, and sanitize all food contact surfaces at least once every four hours. Store in-use utensils clean and dry or wash, rinse, and sanitize at least once every four hours. Cutting board and utensils were washed, rinsed, and sanitized to correct the violation. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed a tray of salmon in the warming cabinet at 114*F. Tray was placed into warmer from the oven, and had been in cabinet for < 30 minutes. The cabinet uses steam vapor to maintain warmth. The water tray was empty, causing unit to be unable of holding at proper temperature. 
CORRECTED = Tray of salmon was placed back into the oven and reheated to 170*F. The water tray in the warming cabinet was refilled. The inside of the cabinet was tested by thermocouple, and was maintaining 141*F. 
Maintain temperatures of all hot Potentially Hazardous Foods at a minimum temperature of 135*F or above. 
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:

CORRECTED = New solutions were made for these containers, then retested for concentration. The concentration was 400ppm of Quat in solution.
Maintain correct concentrations in solutions used to sanitize food contact surfaces.
750-800b To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

Observed the following surfaces to be dusty or soiled: 1) the backsplash of the soda dispenser in the plate prep area of the kitchen - soda splash, 2) the top of the knife holder in the potato prep area - dusty, 3) the top of the knife holder in the Chef's area - crumbs, and 4) the tops of the bulk storage bins in the packaging / wrapping area - dust, spillage.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

Observed cleaned tableware and utensils stored improperly in the following areas: 1) saucers stored face-up in the wait drink-prep station in the dining room, 2) plates stored face-up on the top shelf in the kitchen prep and plating line, and 3) a container of spoons was stored with mouth-contact area facing upward in the wait storage station in the dining room.
Store clean tableware so as to prevent contamination of the eating surface of utensil.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. 

Observed the floors in the following areas to be soiled: 1) under the fryer in the kitchen-lids, boxes; 2) the floor drain under the bar; and 3) the floor of the walk in freezer.   
Clean the floors.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

Observed the mop was stored in the bucket between uses, and the water was soiled. Store used mops hanging upright between uses, and discard mop water after use.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Blue ice scoop holder had buildup of debris in the bottom. Holder and ice scoops were taken to dish area to go through ware washing process.

Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.
**Maintain scoop storage containers clean**

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750-510d Observed an employee switch tasks from handling soiled dishes to clean dishes without properly washing hands. A soapy water dip is not a substitute for handwashing.  The design of the dish room does not lend itself to easy handling of clean dishes. There is a very small drainboard for clean dishes and the dishes must be moved quickly. Use a clean barrier to handle clean dishes when handwashing is not able to be conducted between tasks. Make sure that towels being used as a barrier are kept clean. Discussed handwashing and barrier use with staff and manager. To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

Employee was observed sprinkling parsley over cooked turkey. Employee removed gloves prior to doing this practice and was observed touching face prior to putting hand in the parsley container. Proper handwashing and glove use were discussed with employee. Employees need to be aware of personal habits, and always wash hands after touching any general surfaces (including clothing, glasses, anything on the person) and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. Barriers (i.e. single use gloves, utensils, etc.) must be used as barriers when handling ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: /Wet wiping cloth is laying on the cutting board at sushi and another wet wiping cloth is laying on the wire shelves at sushi. 750-810b Moihot host cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750-800(b) The soda nozzles in the waitress preparation area were observed  coated with mineral and mold accumulation. The following food contact surfaces are soiled: 1) knife block at sushi 2) Dipper well at salad?ice cream area 3) cutting board at rib/hot holding area. The nozzles were cleaned during the inspection. To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

Pizza trays and storage pan were soiled with food debris. All items were taken to dish area to go through ware washing process.
**Clean and sanitize in-use equipment and utensils (i.e. pizza trays, slicer, can opener, etc.) between uses/as needed up to every 4 hours after continuous use to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Dust and debris were observed on the hard plastic mats and shelves underneath where clean glassware was stored at the bar. Clean the hard plastic mats and shelving underneath as needed and maintain it clean to protect cleaned/sanitized glassware from potential contamination.
Clean utensils are observed stored under the right side fryer in contact with oil and grease. Also, clean utensils are observed to be stored in a drawer with tape and other unclean items. 

Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
750-880 Observed the coffee filters to be stored on top of the coffee units in the waitress area. Filters were moved to a drawer during the inspection. 

Observed to go containers stored with food surface up at the bar. Containers were inverted to protect food contact surface.
Observed single use tasting spoons in the salad area stored in a to go container soiled with dust and crumbs. 

Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
750-1120 The wall of fabulous bathrooms and mother's rooms do not have covered garbage cans. All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, covered garbage cans, and be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

Paper towels were not available at bar handsink. Paper towels were provided.
Maintain supplies of soap and paper towels at handsinks to allow for proper handwashing.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: The wall to the right of the sushi cooler has chipped paint. 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair. Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1280 - Personal items (lotion, etc.) were observed with sushi supplies at the bar. Personal items including chicken and lunch left overs were observe in the bottom of the prep cooler at Chinese.  Personal items were removed from the area.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: 750-1310 Observed chemical washing packets being stored in a drawer on the cookline that contained food single-service items (skewers, bag openers). During the inspection, cleaners and a bottle of aspirin were moved from the drawer to another location away from food and single-service articles. Bottles of cleaners observed stored next to single service items in the sushi area. All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed boxes of pizza crusts stored on the floor of the walk in freezer. 
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  
Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed a scoop in the dry bulk container of rice in the dry storage area with the handle touching the product.  
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.
Store food handling utensils properly, with the handle extended out of product.
CORRECTED= Handle was placed out of contact with product.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed that the grille racks and bottom inside of the Vulcan oven was soiled with spillage and grease.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.
Clean the above-referenced equipment as often as necessary.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed that the floor under the dish washing machine and under the 3 compartment sink had some soil. 
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. 
Clean the floors.
CORRECTED= Floor was scrubbed and cleaned during inspection.
